summary: The note surveys the growth of esports from niche online communities to a global industry, covering its history, appeal, economics, and challenges. It discusses misconceptions, inclusivity, player welfare, education and grassroots programs, media integration, and future technologies like VR/AR and cloud gaming. It concludes that addressing fair play, welfare, and inclusivity will support sustainable growth.
one_line: Overview of esports' rise from niche communities to a global industry, with its history, economics, challenges, and future technologies.
key_facts: On October 19, 1972, Stanford University hosted the "Intergalactic Spacewar Olympics," recognized as one of the first instances of competitive gaming.
Dennis "Thresh" Fong won John Carmack's Ferrari in a 1997 "Quake" tournament.
Esports began to resemble today's form in the 1990s with the rise of internet accessibility.
The Mercedes-Benz Arena in Shanghai hosts esports competitions packing tens of thousands of fans.
Samantha Lee, an esports psychologist, says esports provide "a community and a sense of belonging that transcends physical boundaries."
Dr. Alex Ramirez's research on September 15, 2023 found that gaming can enhance cognitive abilities, problem-solving skills, and social interaction when engaged responsibly.
The Anti-Harassment Initiative was launched in October 2023 to address sexism and harassment in the esports community.
The High-Tech Esports Training Complex was unveiled in New York on September 30, 2023.
As of September 2023, the National Collegiate Esports Association reported an increase in scholarships awarded to esports athletes.
Amanda Chen heads a youth esports league established in November 2023.
Michael "Shroud" Grzesiek retired due to health concerns, highlighting burnout and unhealthy gaming practices.
Louis Vuitton partnered with "League of Legends" for the World Championship in September 2023.
ESPN has begun broadcasting major esports tournaments, and discussion of including esports in the Olympic program continues as of September 2023.
Google plans to launch a cloud gaming platform in December 2023, which could remove hardware barriers.
Lisa Brooks, a beverage company executive, says esports offers "a direct channel to tech-savvy, engaged audiences."
